dataset.name: Porewater chemistry in Typha-dominated brackish tidal marsh, PIE LTER, Plum Island Sound, MA, July 2022–September 2024
description: This dataset contains profile measurements of porewater constituents taken on 3-4 days across the growing seasons in 2022, 2023, and 2024 in a tidal brackish marsh within the Plum Island Ecosystems Long Term Ecological Research site (PIE LTER), located in the Plum Island Sound, Massachusetts (MA). Measurements were taken to monitor changes in porewater chemistry induced by seasonal saltwater intrusion at the site. Samples were taken in two locations: one was close to the creek bank and the other in the marsh interior. Water was sampled from 2-5 depths between the surface to 50cm using a sipper consisting of a hollow stainless steel rod with an opening at the end similar to that described in (Berg & McGlathery, 2001). The rod was pushed into the sediment to the desired depth, typically every 10cm, and water samples were taken by syringe. Water was not obtained at all depths. Samples were preserved and analyzed in the lab. Metadata files Typha_porewater_sipper_dd.csv and Typha_porewater_sipper_flmd.csv contain detailed information on data variables, sampling and QA/QC methods, and site location.

measurementTechnique:
Porewater profiles [Fe, SO4, Cl, PO4, CH4, NH4, HS] were taken on three to four days throughout the growing season. Water was sampled from 2-5 depths between the surface to 50cm using a sipper consisting of a hollow stainless-steel rod with an opening at the end similar to that described in (Berg & McGlthery, 2001). The rod was pushed into the sediment to the desired depth, typically every 10cm, and water samples were taken by syringe. Water was not obtained at all depths. The initial 5 ml were discarded, before separate samples for gases, redox sensitive elements and nutrients were taken. Analyses are conducted according to PIE-LTER protocols. Sample preparation for SO4 analysis differed in 2022 and 2023: In 2022, samples were filtered into a scintillation vial and 0.5ml were placed into 9.5ml of DI for the analysis on an ion chromatograph. In this year, sulfides were not removed because we had been working on the assumption that sulfide concentrations would be very low. However, we found the sulfide concentrations to be higher than expected, sometimes over 1mM. In 2023, we carefully filtered the porewater into a 6ml exetainer and sealed it in the field so that the sample was not exposed to oxygen. In the laboratory, a sample was taken for SO4 and Cl and diluted as before but the sample was immediately purged with N2 to remove sulfides. Due to some possible re-oxidation of sulfides in 2022 values may be overestimated.
Flags are used to identify samples with special conditions: NS indicates that there was no sample to analyze either because there was no sample or because there was not enough sample. SL indicates that the sample was lost, e.g. due to spillage or a container breaking. C indicates that the value should be used with caution, e.g. because of a difference in sample storage or preservation to the other samples, a cracked container, and/or the value being outside a previously observed range. BD indicates that the value is bellow detection but above 0. BD_Z indicates that based on the standard curve, the estimated value was negative and has been set to 0. X_ACC indicates that the QA/QC targets for accuracy for that value were exceeded. X_PREC indicates that the QA/QC targets for precision for that value were exceeded. X_RNG indicates that the value is outside the range of standards or calibration. S_COMP indicates that the sample composition was unlike the rest for this analyte.
